newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's central bank issues wages warning.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's central bank issues wages warning.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal on Monday warned the Socialist government that it must severely limit wage rises in 1997 to meet the ambitious inflation target.
The 2.25-2.75 percent inflation goal for next year was attainable but only..."with strong salary restraint," the central bank said in its latest economic report.

The government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres has admitted that cutting inflation sufficiently is going to be the biggest challenge in preparing the economy for the European Union's planned single currency.
The rolling 12-month rate, which the government uses as its yardstick, was running at 3.4 percent in September. The central bank forecast it would fall to 3.25 percent by the end of the year.

Analysts say a rate above three percent next year would jeopardise the country's chances of making the grade for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) for which entry will be decided on the basis of 1997 economic performance.

The central bank's report was released as the Communist-led Common Front union alliance, the country's largest, prepared to take on the government over its offer of a public sector wage rise of 2.38 percent for next year.

The Bank said that there was probably not much more the government could do to reduce prices growth before the first quarter of next year but a big effort would be needed over the final nine months of 1997.

"The recent trend in consumer prices and the outlook until the end of the year show there will be some resistance to be overcome (to reduce) average inflation up till the end of the first quarter of 1997," it said.
But the Bank had some good news too. It raised slightly its forecast for economic growth in 1996 to 2.25-2.75 percent, from the 1.75-2.75 percent seen previously.
The Bank said that economic growth in 1996 would be around one percentage point higher than the expected average for the European Union as a whole.
